The wild cluster bootstrap for a difference in differences with few clusters

Source: R/panel_causal.R
wcb.Rd

A p-value and confidence interval for the treatment effect of plndid that stay accurate when there are few clusters (a policy assigned to a handful of districts or states), where the cluster-robust t test over-rejects.

Usage

wcb(
  data,
  unit,
  time,
  y,
  trtd,
  covs = NULL,
  cl = NULL,
  reps = 9999L,
  wtype = c("rademacher", "webb"),
  seed = NULL,
  ties = c("count", "strict"),
  conflvl = 0.95
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per unit and period.

unit, time, y

Column names: the unit, the period (numeric, for example a year or a month index) and the outcome.

trtd

Column name of the treatment indicator (0 or 1).

covs

Optional column names of time-varying controls.

cl

Column name of the clusters (default the unit), or two column names for two-way clustering (Cameron, Gelbach and Miller 2011): \(V_a + V_b - V_{ab}\), each term with the small-sample factor of the dimension with fewer clusters, and t on its \(G - 1\) degrees of freedom. A composite cluster (district by month, say) is one column made with interaction().

reps

Bootstrap replications (default 9999).

wtype

"rademacher" (default) or "webb".

seed

Optional seed.

ties

"count" (default) or "strict": whether a bootstrap \(|t^*|\) equal to \(|t|\) counts against the null.

conflvl

Confidence level (default 0.95).

Value

A data frame of class rmbl_wild with the columns estimate, t, p_value, lower, upper, clusters, draws and enumerated.

Details

This is the restricted wild cluster bootstrap (WCR) of Cameron, Gelbach and Miller (2008). The model is fitted with the null \(\beta = \beta_0\) imposed; each bootstrap outcome is the restricted fit plus its residuals multiplied, cluster by cluster, by a random sign (Rademacher) or by one of Webb's six values; the cluster-robust t statistic is recomputed each time. The p-value is the share of bootstrap \(|t^*|\) at least \(|t|\). With ties = "count" (the default) a draw that equals \(|t|\) counts: the sign patterns that reproduce the data are among the draws, as the observed assignment is in a permutation test, and the test is exact at its level. With "strict" only draws above \(|t|\) count, as fwildclusterboot does; under full enumeration this gives a smaller p-value (the two sign patterns that reproduce \(|t|\) are left out). With Rademacher weights and \(2^G \le\) reps every sign pattern is enumerated (as fwildclusterboot does); with very few clusters (under about 12) Webb's weights, which have more distinct values, are better. The interval collects the \(\beta_0\) not rejected at \(1 -\) conflvl, found by bisection with the same draws; it is unbounded when no value can be rejected (with Rademacher weights and \(G\) clusters the smallest attainable p-value is \(2/2^G\), so four clusters can never reject at 5%: that is the honest answer, not a failure of the method).

References

Cameron AC, Gelbach JB, Miller DL (2008). Bootstrap-based improvements for inference with clustered errors. Review of Economics and Statistics 90(3):414-427. doi:10.1162/rest.90.3.414

Webb MD (2023). Reworking wild bootstrap-based inference for clustered errors. Canadian Journal of Economics 56(3):839-858. doi:10.1111/caje.12661

Roodman D, Nielsen MO, MacKinnon JG, Webb MD (2019). Fast and wild: bootstrap inference in Stata using boottest. The Stata Journal 19(1):4-60. doi:10.1177/1536867X19830877

Examples

p <- polex()
# the reform was assigned to four regions: four clusters
wcb(p, "district", "month", "crmrate", "reformed",
                       cl = "region", wtype = "webb", reps = 99,
                       seed = 1)
#>   estimate         t    p_value     lower     upper clusters draws enumerated
#> 1 -3.23164 -19.51674 0.01010101 -3.563541 -2.910293        4    99      FALSE
